# std/for

> Counting loop over an inclusive range: for i = a to b ... end

truck [std](../std.md) · [source](../../../registry/std/for.pkg)

```
for i = 1 to 5
  print i * i
end
```

`for` has no backend of its own. It is built entirely from other `std`
packages, which is why it `needs` them:

```
let i = a
while i <= b
  ...
  i = i + 1
end
```

Because it is an expansion:

- the loop variable is declared in the surrounding block and stays visible
  after the loop;
- the upper bound is re-evaluated on every iteration;
- `to` is a keyword and cannot be used as a variable name.

## Syntax

Kind: `statement`

```
for {i: newvar} = {from: expr int} to {to: expr int} {body: block} end
```

| slot | takes | type |
|---|---|---|
| `i` | new variable name | any |
| `from` | expression | `int` |
| `to` | expression | `int` |
| `body` | block of statements | — |

## Expands to

This package has no backend: each use is rewritten to the following
source, with `{slot}` replaced by what was written there, and compiled again.

```
let {i} = {from}
while {i} <= {to}
{body}
{i} = {i} + 1
end
```
